subject: Catalyst Retail: holiday campaign traffic plan & temporary throughput handoff
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Catalyst Retail: holiday campaign traffic plan & temporary throughput handoff

Team — looping you all in on Catalyst's upcoming holiday push. They asked today for a temporary throughput increase window and a clear execution plan so their engineering and ops teams can disable client-side throttles. Summary: Catalyst expects a concentrated 12-hour peak on 2026-11-25 (Black Friday) with an estimated burst up to 6x baseline RPS for their storefront personalization calls (avg seq len ~420 tokens). They want: a) a temporary rate uplift for that 12-hour window, b) an agreed canary + rollback plan, and c) clarity on billing/overage handling.

Attachments: catalyst_hol_launch_forecast_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet) — forecast by hour and endpoints.

Asks:
- Aditya / infra: can we support a 6x short-duration bump with our current routing? If not, what minimal capacity reservation or routing override is needed?
- Lauren / sales: confirm billing approach for a short-term uplift (e.g., usage + pre-agreed overage multiplier or short-term dedicated pool billing).
- Mina / AM: confirm Catalyst's contract owner and PO timeline — they want this committed in writing by Sept 1.

I put a draft mutual action plan on Drive (link below). Goal this week: agree on what we can commit to (capacity & canary) so I can get back to their CFO and SRE.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks for the heads up. Finance flagged that we need an explicit billing route: either bill actual usage against their committed tiers + overage at 1.5x, or pre-purchase a short-term Dedicated slot for the 12 hours and invoice as "burst entitlement". I'll ask FP&A for rough margin calc on both and share by EOD Friday.

Catalyst legal will likely need the timeframe spelled out in an amendment — Mina, do you have the SOW/contract owner? I can draft amendment language.

—Lauren

lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 12:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Catalyst Retail: holiday campaign traffic plan & temporary throughput handoff

Quick technical questions so we can size properly:
- Endpoint(s) involved? (Is this text-generation chat vs. short completion vs embeddings?).
- Expected tokens per request (you mentioned ~420 mean but need distribution — p95/p99).
- Do they use streaming? Streaming increases connection count which affects proxy limits.
- Are they ok with a phased canary (10% -> 50% -> full) over 90 minutes?

Prelim thoughts: a sustained 6x RPS at 420 tokens will stress both serving and KV memory (KV cache pressure). If they use our hosted tier, we can do a temporary routing override to route to higher-priority pools and enable dynamic batching settings for that window. Worst-case recommendation: reserve a Dedicated burst pool (N GPUs) for the 12 hours — that gives predictable latency and isolation but requires procurement signoff.

I added a short technical checklist to the Drive doc. Need Carlos/Elena to confirm endpoint types and p95 token size by Friday so we can finalize capacity ask.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@catalystretail.com>

Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 16:29:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Catalyst Retail: holiday campaign traffic plan & temporary throughput handoff

Thanks Sean — confirming endpoints: storefront-personalize (text completion API) and recommendations-rerank (batch reranking embeddings). Typical request sizes: personalize avg 420 tokens, p95 890, embeddings requests small but high cardinality. We do use streaming for personalize.

We've attached an internal hourly forecast and can sign an amendment. Attachment: catalyst_hol_launch_forecast_v2.xlsx.

Can we agree to a 3-step canary (10% / 50% / 100%) over 2 hours on the day of? If Dedicated burst is needed, we can authorize payment if you provide SKU and estimate.

Regards,
Carlos

Head of Platform Engineering, Catalyst Retail

Following up on procurement: Catalyst's procurement lead is Elena Park (cc'd). She confirmed they can sign an amendment but need the exact hours and expected units for billing. CFO wants the total estimated spend before sign-off.

Action items for us:
- Aditya: provide a minimal Dedicated SKU + estimated token/unit count for the 12-hour peak. If we can do routing override instead, provide expected latency/p99 impact and a best-effort cost estimate.
- Lauren: draft amendment template and the short-term overage billing options.
- Sean: agree to a communication plan and canary timings so I can pass to Elena's procurement team.

I attached a redlined MAP (mutual_action_plan_Catalyst_2026.pdf).

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 17:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Catalyst Retail: holiday campaign traffic plan & temporary throughput handoff

Engineering can support a routed bump without a Dedicated purchase for up to ~3x baseline with degraded p99 latency (we can keep p50/p95 stable). For 6x we recommend a short Dedicated burst for 12 hours: estimate 4 A100-equivalent GPUs for that window. Rough cost for customer (list price) ~ $34k for the 12-hour block (including one-off setup). If Catalyst prefers routing-only, we'll propose a staged canary: 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 3 hours with an automated fallback at any error rate >1.8% or p99 > 1500ms.

I'll upload the exact SKU and a cost worksheet to the Drive link and leave notes on rollback hooks. Once we have their sign-off on the hours I can lock the allocation.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
